newsitem.title: USA: Timberland sees difficult start to 1997.
newsitem.headline: Timberland sees difficult start to 1997.

text.p: Timberland Co Chief Financial Officer Keith Monda said it will be difficult for the footwear manufacturer to follow up its record fourth quarter net income with a profitable 1997 first half.

"Given our strong seasonality and the increasing percentage of retail business, with the higher level of retail costs, it is difficult to achieve a profit in the first half of the year," Monda told analysts and reporters on a conference call.
Earlier, Timberland reported record revenues and net income in its fourth quarter.
Chief Operating Officer Jeffrey Swartz said a focus in 1997 will be enhancing and "cleaning up" its distribution program by moving to a higher quality but smaller network.

"Eliminating unprofitable, non-brand enhancing distribution is a strong signal to consumers and shareholders at the same time that this company is willing to endure short-term revenue losses in certain markets in order to ensure the long-term power, growth and power of the Timberland brand," he said. Timberland will renovate and expand its store in New York City this year and will add to its string of 71 owned and operated stores, he said.
Timberland will narrow the number of department stores it serves to fewer, higher quality stores, Swartz said.

He said Timberland will also continue to improve its operations, which have hindered the company's strong sales in the past. Timberland has strengthened management, cut the number of distribution centers and has invested in operating systems, he said.

"We still turn our inventory less effectively than our competitors," he said. "Our lead times are still long, and our ability to forecast demand for our products (is) less capable than it needs to be," he added.

Fourth quarter sales were driven by a rise in domestic sales of $48 million from last year's fourth quarter to $175.8 million. That more than offset a drop of $2.7 million to $45.3 million in international sales, Monda said.
Worldwide apparel and accessory revenues rose $14.8 million from last year to $58.5 million in the fourth quarter, he said.

Gross margins rose in the fourth quarter to 37.3 percent, up 3.9 points from last year, due to savings from the company's expanded and enhanced sourcing efforts, improved manufacturing efficiencies resulting from its 1995 restructuring, and cuts in sales returns, he said.
Gross margins for the year rose to 36.5 percent from 31 percent in 1995, Monda said.
